hooks.text: A cosmic structure ten billion light-years long shouldn't exist.
Something spans ten percent of the entire observable universe.
Our models say this ten billion light-year structure is impossible.

title: The Cosmic Wall That Defies Physics
description: The Hercules-Corona Borealis Great Wall is so massive that it challenges everything we know about the universe.

beats.text: A cosmic structure ten billion light-years long shouldn't exist.
beats.visual: Artist concept of a vast galaxy filament superstructure

beats.text: In 2013, astronomer Istvan Horvath and his team mapped the locations of massive explosions called gamma-ray bursts.
beats.visual: Artist concept of a gamma-ray burst from a dying massive star

beats.text: Using data from NASA's Swift satellite, they found an unprecedented cluster of bursts near the constellation Hercules.
beats.visual: NASA Swift Gamma-Ray Burst Mission spacecraft artist concept

beats.text: This cluster revealed a superstructure spanning ten billion light-years, roughly ten percent of the observable universe.
beats.visual: Cosmic web Millennium Simulation showing matter distribution

beats.text: Strangely, this behemoth was named the Hercules-Corona Borealis Great Wall by a Filipino teenager on Wikipedia.
beats.visual: Wikipedia website logo on a screen

beats.text: But some astronomers argue this giant record-breaker might not even be real.
beats.visual: Swift BAT all-sky gamma-ray burst distribution map
queries: all sky map gamma ray bursts

beats.text: They believe it could be a statistical illusion, leaving its existence to be proven by future telescopes.
beats.visual: Conceptual design of the proposed THESEUS space telescope mission

beats.text: Until then, we are left with a cosmic structure ten billion light-years long that shouldn't exist.
beats.visual: Large scale structure galaxy wall illustration
